Thursday night
Our flatmate Devesh has been trying to sell his old phone for two weeks. He's asking eighteen thousand. Kavitha and I looked it up: the same model, used, sells for around eight. Tonight a buyer came over, a college student with exact cash. She offered nine. Devesh looked offended. "Nine? It still has the original box!" The student left. Kavitha whispered to me, "He'd never pay eighteen for it himself." So after dinner I asked him, gently, "Devesh, if you were buying this today, what would you pay?" He was quiet for a long time, turning the phone over. "Honestly? Ten." Then he laughed at himself a little. "Why does it feel worth more when it's mine?" I didn't have an answer. He's relisting it at ten tomorrow. I wrote this down because I have a whole shelf of old stuff I think is priceless too.
Shalini
